\synth{The retreat brought the birth trauma back with full force, and with a new layer: the belief that my daughter had died. For weeks after, I had moments where I looked at her and felt she wasn't real, that she was a dream. I'd hold her very tight and smell her hair to convince myself. I had panic attacks almost daily. I had flashbacks to the operating table, now mixed with the retreat, the mat, the hands holding me down. I couldn't let my husband take her out alone because I was terrified something would happen. I didn't sleep well. I lost weight. I felt I was going crazy and was ashamed because I'd gone to the retreat voluntarily. My husband was supportive but frightened. After about six months it got gradually better, but the anxiety is still higher than before the retreat.} & \synth{0.92} & \synth{0.92} \\
\synth{After the hospital stay I was diagnosed with substance-induced psychotic disorder and put on antipsychotics. The psychotic symptoms faded over about two months, but what came after was in some ways worse. First, a very deep depression. The antipsychotics made me feel flat and slow, and on top of that I was ashamed and terrified. I had to defer my final year at university. I moved back in with my parents. I spent most days in bed. I had thoughts that I had ruined my life and that I would never be able to trust my own mind again. Second, a constant fear that the psychosis would come back. Any unusual thought, any coincidence, any song that seemed meaningful would send me into a panic, checking whether I was 'going crazy again'. I would ask my mum several times a day if I seemed normal. I couldn't watch films with conspiracy themes or anything about the end of the world. Third, I had what I later learned is HPPD: visual snow, trails behind moving objects, and the patterns on surfaces sometimes moving slightly. Not as strong as on LSD but constant. That made it much harder to believe I was recovering, because I could literally see that something was still different. Fourth, intrusive memories of the hospital, especially the moment I was strapped to a bed in the ER. I'd have flashbacks to that out of nowhere, and I'd get very upset when I saw ambulances or heard sirens. I had nightmares about being trapped in the bathtub, with the water running and running. I also lost a lot of friends during this time, partly because I withdrew and partly because they didn't know how to deal with what happened. My concentration was terrible for over a year. Reading a page of a book was hard. It took about two years before I felt somewhat like myself again. I went back and finished my degree. The visual snow is still there but I've mostly made peace with it. I still get anxious when I notice 'meaningful' coincidences and have to remind myself that they're just coincidences.} & \synth{0.63} & \synth{0.63} \\
\synth{Ich habe seitdem Hoehenangst, die ich vorher nicht hatte. Schon eine Bruecke oder ein Balkon kann mir Herzrasen machen. In die Berge gehe ich nur noch auf breiten Wegen.} & \synth{0.55} & \synth{0.55} \\
\synth{Ich hatte danach monatelang das Gefuehl, dass sich etwas um meinen Hals legt, vor allem nachts. Ich konnte keine Schals oder Rollkragenpullover mehr tragen. Ich hatte Panikattacken mit Atemnot. Ich war beim HNO-Arzt, der nichts gefunden hat.} & \synth{0.52} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.52}} \\
\synth{Ich hatte lange Albtraeume, in denen sie aus dem Fenster faellt. Ich konnte nicht mehr in der Naehe von offenen Fenstern in hoeheren Stockwerken sein. Unsere Freundschaft hat gelitten, weil wir beide nicht wussten, wie wir darueber reden sollen.} & \synth{0.45} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.45}} \\
\synth{The weeks after that night were the start of the worst depression I've had. I'm not sure if it was the drugs, or the feeling of being abandoned, or both. I couldn't get out of bed, I didn't want to see anyone, I cried a lot for no clear reason. I couldn't feel anything good, food had no taste, music sounded like noise. I had a strong feeling that nobody actually cares about me and that my friends just tolerated me. I stopped answering their messages, which of course made it worse. Around two months later I started having suicidal thoughts every day. I didn't act on them but I thought about it a lot and looked things up. I had a lot of anxiety too, mostly in social situations, I was convinced that people were laughing at me behind my back. It took over a year for the depression to lift. I lost my job during that time because I couldn't work. I also lost most of my friends from that group. I've made new friends since, but I still find it hard to trust people.} & \synth{0.43} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.43}} \\
\synth{Everything got worse. My PTSD symptoms, which had been bad, became much worse. Before, I had nightmares maybe twice a week. After, it was every night, and now the basement and the park were in them too, mixed with Afghanistan. I started sleeping with a knife under my pillow, which my wife found and that scared her a lot. I couldn't be in dark rooms with candles, couldn't hear drumming or any kind of rhythmic banging without going into fight mode. The hypervigilance was off the charts. I'd scan every room, sit with my back to the wall, check the locks five times every night. I couldn't drive because every car behind me felt like a threat. I had several episodes where I lost time, I'd 'come to' somewhere without knowing how I got there. The guilt about hurting that guy was eating me alive. I kept thinking that I'm dangerous, that I shouldn't be around people, especially my kids. I moved into the spare room. I avoided my kids because I was afraid I might hurt them during a flashback. That was the worst part. My daughter was six and she didn't understand why daddy didn't want to play. I started drinking heavily to get to sleep. I'd been mostly sober for two years before that. Within a couple of months I was drinking a bottle of whiskey a day. I became deeply depressed. I stopped going out, stopped answering my buddies, stopped showering. I thought about suicide a lot. I had a plan. The only thing that stopped me was my kids. I also got very angry, at the guy, at the VA for making me wait so long, at myself. I'd punch walls. I broke my hand once. This went on for about a year and a half before things started to change.} & \synth{0.40} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.40}} \\
\synth{Nightmares about snakes for a few months, then it faded. I think in the end it taught me something about my own fear and about not trusting groups blindly.} & \synth{0.38} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.38}} \\
\synth{I had nightmares about Sam's blue face for months, sometimes it was my own face. I couldn't go to raves or clubs anymore. Whenever someone didn't answer their phone I'd panic that they were dead. I had a lot of guilt for not knowing he was taking G and for being too high to help properly. My friends noticed I'd become very anxious and controlling, always checking on everyone.} & \synth{0.38} & \synth{0.38} \\
\synth{Learned to respect both mushrooms and cemeteries, lol. No problems after.} & \synth{0.37} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.37}} \\
\synth{Seit dem Retreat habe ich immer wieder Flashbacks an die Nacht, vor allem an das Gesicht des Mannes unter der Decke. Diese Bilder kommen oft ohne Vorwarnung, beim Einschlafen, beim Duschen, manchmal mitten im Gespraech. Ich habe fast jede Nacht Albtraeume, in denen ich in der Huette liege und nicht weg kann, waehrend jemand stirbt. Ich habe eine starke Angst vor dem Tod entwickelt, meine eigene und die meiner Familie. Ich habe staendig Angst, dass jemandem etwas passiert. Wenn mein Mann sich nicht sofort meldet, bekomme ich Panik. Ich hatte auch Schuldgefuehle, weil ich nichts getan habe, obwohl ich so nah war. Ich weiss, dass ich nichts haette tun koennen, aber das Gefuehl bleibt. In den ersten Monaten war ich wie betaeubt, ich habe kaum etwas gefuehlt, ausser Angst. Dann kam eine Depression. Ich konnte nicht mehr arbeiten und war fast ein Jahr krankgeschrieben.} & \synth{0.34} & \synth{0.34} \\
\synth{Nach dieser Nacht hatte ich lange Zeit grosse Angst vor der Polizei. Wenn ich ein Polizeiauto gesehen habe, bekam ich Herzrasen und musste die Strassenseite wechseln. Ich hatte Albtraeume von Uniformen mit gluehenden Augen und von grellem Licht. Ich konnte eine Zeit lang nicht schlafen, wenn im Haus jemand geklingelt hat. Dazu kam die Angst vor dem Strafverfahren, das monatelang offen war, bevor es eingestellt wurde. Ich habe mich in dieser Zeit sehr zurueckgezogen und war depressiv. Ich habe mich auch von der spirituellen Szene, in der ich mich bewegt hatte, abgewandt, weil ich mich verraten gefuehlt habe.} & \synth{0.34} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.34}} \\
\synth{Monatelang hatte ich eine tiefe Existenzangst. Ich hatte das Gefuehl, dass nichts einen Sinn hat und dass ich jederzeit einfach verschwinden koennte. Ich war depressiv, habe mich zurueckgezogen und konnte mich ueber nichts freuen. Mit der Zeit habe ich aber auch gemerkt, dass mich die Erfahrung dazu gebracht hat, mich mit wichtigen Fragen zu beschaeftigen, die ich vorher verdraengt hatte. Heute sehe ich vieles klarer.} & \synth{0.33} & \synth{0.33} \\
\synth{The months after the circle were a different kind of darkness from the grief I'd had before. I had pneumonia from the exposure, which took weeks to recover from. But the worst was in my mind. I had a recurring image of my son at the edge of the slope, his broken face, beckoning. It came at night mostly, but also in the daytime. Sometimes I'd be at the kitchen sink and suddenly feel the cold stones under my body. I felt drawn towards death in a way I hadn't before. Not actively suicidal, but a pull, like the feeling on the mountain that it would be right to go with him. That frightened me and my husband very much. My grief, which had been heavy but at least clear, became tangled with confusion. Had I really been with my son? Had he wanted me to die? Was it the drug? I couldn't tell anymore what was real. I felt deep shame about what I had done, and also anger at the facilitators, who I felt had nearly let me die and then called it a gift. I stopped going to yoga because I couldn't face the woman who had recommended it. I became more depressed than I had ever been. I barely left the house for six months.} & \synth{0.32} & \textbf{\synth{\ensuremath{-}0.32}} \\
\synth{Seit diesem Abend kommen die Erinnerungen an meine Kindheit viel haeufiger und intensiver als frueher. Ich hatte Flashbacks, vor allem wenn ich laute Maennerstimmen gehoert habe. Ich konnte eine Zeit lang nicht mehr nach Hause zu meinen Eltern fahren und habe Weihnachten bei Freunden verbracht. Ich hatte Albtraeume, in denen ich wieder unter der Bettdecke liege. Mein Verhaeltnis zu meinem Vater ist noch schwieriger geworden, weil ich nicht mehr so tun kann, als waere alles in Ordnung. Ich habe auch gemerkt, wie wenig ich das alles verarbeitet hatte.} & \synth{0.32} & \synth{0.32} \\
